question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosine function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcosh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-8\operatorname{arcosh}⁡\sqrt{x}) \\  & =-8\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcosh}⁡\sqrt{x}) \\  & =-8\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{{(\sqrt{x})}^{2}-1}}\cdot {(\sqrt{x})}^{′} \\  & =-8\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{x-1}}\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} \\  & =-\frac{4}{\sqrt{x(x-1)}}.\end{aligned}
$$
